title: Connected-platform worked vectors (ADR 0006 §5.6)
description: Machine-readable worked examples of the contract: each vector is a scenario script (given + steps) with expected gate decisions and pending-effect states, consumed by both Cadence's and AgenticOS's test suites. Step `expect` objects are a closed vocabulary — every key is enumerated below so a typo fails schema validation. `expect.record` embeds pending-effect record specimens, each validated separately against pending-effect.schema.json.

$schema.description: Inert annotation: a URI naming the schema this document claims.

presser.description: The decision.by shape: who pressed, their role, the rule that authorised it.

expect.description: Assertions on gate decision and pending-effect state after the step. Absent keys are not asserted.

result.description: call steps only. executed: ran through the proxy at once. staged: parked as a pending effect, caller got `staged` + effect_id. existing: a retried open with the same caller-named handle deduped to the already-staged effect (same effect_id, no second row). error: the platform call was attempted and errored.

press.description: press steps only. refused: the press did not take (terminal row, unauthorised presser, or missing effect).

effect_id.description: call steps only: the staged result carried an effect_id.

state.description: State of the pending-effect row this step produced (call) or acted on (press/edit_source) after the step. null asserts the step produced no row. For restart/caller_deadline steps it asserts the row the vector is tracking.

close_reason.description: The reason named on a closed row (e.g. source_changed).

fired.description: Whether this step caused platform traffic for the staged call — the "decline never fires" / "never re-fires" assertion.

executions.description: Cumulative platform executions for the pending effect after this step — the exactly-once counter (§5.4 step 9).

needs_you.description: Whether a Needs-you item was raised (verified:false raises one; §5.4 step 6).

delivered.description: The outcome arrived as a message to the task or PM — never only to a waiter (C5, §5.4 step 6).

wait.description: caller_deadline steps: the caller's wait ended while the durable row persists.

record.description: A pending-effect record specimen for the state at this point in the lifecycle; consumers validate it against pending-effect.schema.json.

contract.description: Contract anchors the vector exercises (C-numbers and/or §-refs of ADR 0006).

tool_table.description: The adapter's declared table for this scenario: the string "default" resolves to fake-tool-table.json shipped beside this file, or an inline object (which may be deliberately malformed when table_valid is false).

table_valid.description: Default true. When true, the tool_table must validate against tool-table.schema.json; when false it must fail — the fixture harness asserts the direction both ways.

reported_manifest_version.description: The manifest version the platform reports now — the platform side, never a call argument. Explicit null means the platform declares none (undeclared → gates as send). When the key is omitted the table's own manifest_version is reported.

agent.description: The calling agent alias (connection-derived at runtime; named here for the record specimen).

account.description: The enrolled account handle the call runs under.

sources.description: Reviewed source artifacts preloaded into the fake platform, name → content. A send may pin one via input.source; its sha256 becomes the row's source_hash.

adapter.description: Fake-adapter behaviour knobs — deterministic platform responses.

read_back.description: What the platform's post-execution read-back reports: verify compares applied state to the approved input; mismatch simulates divergence (verified:false); unknown models a platform with no read-back.

fail.description: The named tool's platform call errors with this message.

step.description: One scenario action plus its expected gate/row assertions, discriminated by `action`.

arguments.description: The call arguments. An `effect` key here is ignored by the gate (C2). May name a source artifact via `source`.

handle.description: Caller-named request handle; a retry with the same handle dedupes (existing:true).

crash_after_decision.description: Model the restart-inside-the-window case: the decision is recorded durably, then the daemon dies before execution/outcome (§5.4 step 8). The next restart step reconciles the row.

uncaught.description: The edit lands without the waiting-row cancel scan noticing — models the race §5.4 step 3 covers with the re-check inside Execute.
